items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon mountain characters, short and punchy: a smug pompous Mount Everest, and a chill relaxed deadpan volcano called Chimborazo.
lines: You think Everest is the highest point on Earth.
But stand here... and you're two kilometres closer to space, and to the Sun.
[chill, friendly, relaxed] Hi. You're standing on me.
A sleepy volcano in Ecuador, about two thousand six hundred metres shorter than Everest.
So how is the shorter mountain closer to the stars?
Rewind to eighteen oh two, when many thought Chimborazo was Earth's highest mountain.
Explorer Alexander von Hoom-bolt climbed to about five thousand, eight hundred seventy-five metres, higher than any European before.
Then... altitude sickness sent him back down.
[chill, deadpan] I have that effect on people.
In the eighteen fifties, surveyors in India measured the Himalayas, and Chimborazo got demoted.
So how did the loser end up closest to space?
Because Earth isn't a perfect ball. It spins, so it bulges at the equator.
The equator sits about twenty-one kilometres farther from the centre than the poles. ... Earth has a belly.
And Chimborazo sits just one degree from the equator. Ecuador literally means equator. Everest? About twenty-eight degrees north.
Measured from Earth's centre, Chimborazo's peak is six thousand, three hundred eighty-four kilometres out. Everest's: six thousand, three hundred eighty-two.
Everest wins from the sea. ... Chimborazo wins from the core.
Here's the twist: Everest isn't even in the top twenty.
So who's on top of the world? Depends where you measure from.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
